compiled_state.description:
## Problem
The Gerrit LLM-Review comment (`review_bot/adapter.py::_translate_findings`) and three CLI
text renderers (`_cli/_llm_commands.py`: plan-review advisory findings, code-review findings,
completion-verdict findings) print the `severity` label to the human reviewer. Per the
epic's ADR decision, the human-facing signal becomes blocking/advisory only (no raw priority
number, no severity label). `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` is duplicated byte-for-byte in
`code_review/shim.py` and `review_bot/adapter.py`; both copies exist solely to feed the
label this ticket removes.

## Approach
1. In `review_bot/adapter.py::_translate_findings`, replace the `severity` key in each
   translated finding dict with a `blocking: bool` (a finding present in `verdict["blocking"]`
   vs `verdict["advisory"]`). Delete `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` from `adapter.py`.
2. Delete `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` from `code_review/shim.py`'s `_to_common_finding`
   likewise -- the common-finding shape now carries `priority`/`decision` from the prior
   ticket, not a mapped severity label.
3. Update the Gerrit comment body builder (`render_findings_block`/`_summarize`) to show
   `[BLOCKING]`/`[advisory]` per finding instead of an uppercased severity word.
4. Update the three CLI renderers in `_llm_commands.py` (`_render_plan_review_text`,
   `_render_review_text`, `_render_verdict_text`) to print `BLOCKING`/`ADVISORY` (derived from
   `decision`/`blocking` on the finding) instead of `f.get('severity')`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `grep -rn "_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY" src/` returns no matches.
- [ ] The rendered Gerrit comment body for a sample verdict shows `BLOCKING` or `advisory` per
  finding and never a severity word (critical/major/minor/high/medium/low/info).
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k translate_findings` and the adapter's
  comment-rendering tests pass with updated assertions on the new tag text.
- [ ] The `_llm_commands.py` renderer test module (locate via
  `pytest --collect-only -q -k llm_commands`) passes with updated assertions for
  `_render_plan_review_text`, `_render_review_text`, and `_render_verdict_text`.

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit tests against the real rendering functions, fed a production-shaped
verdict dict (contract test). Oracle: the exact rendered string contains `BLOCKING`/`advisory`
tokens and none of the retired severity words. Refactoring litmus: renaming an internal
helper inside the renderer must not break these tests, since they assert on the printed
text, not on which helper produced it.
compiled_state.title: Surface blocking/advisory instead of severity in review-bot and CLI renderers
